items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And he was telling me about the old Fletcher Henderson band.

ctx.x: They had a lot of head arrangements, yeah. “Jumpin’ at the Woodside” at first it wasn’t even written out I heard.

Yeah. Oddly enough, I don’t think only that, I had a long conversation with Teddy Wilson one night, flying across the Atlantic believe it or not. And he was telling me about the old Fletcher Henderson band. This is slightly off the subject. But he went down this list of tunes, we got to talking about head arrangements. And all those things, like “King Porter Stomp” and “Big John Special”—
I remember “Big John Special.” “King Porter Stomp” is pretty complicated to be a head arrangement.
